hero.headline: Indian River County schools superintendent to step down June 2027
hero.teaser: School District of Indian River County Superintendent Dr. Moore announced Wednesday he will conclude his tenure with the district effective June 30, 2027, after nearly seven years
hero.body:
School District of Indian River County Superintendent Dr. Moore announced Wednesday he will conclude his tenure with the district effective June 30, 2027, after nearly seven years of service. Moore, whose tenure currently ranks as the second longest among Florida's appointed district school superintendents, shared his decision with school board members and his Cabinet Leadership Team before informing district and school leaders and broader staff.

During Moore's time leading the district, the School District of Indian River County advanced from 38th to 5th among Florida's 67 school districts based on District Grade and earned 4 consecutive A district grades. The district grew the share of schools earning an A or B from 47 percent to 100 percent and achieved a 96 percent high school graduation rate. The district was named the No. 1 Best Place to Teach in Florida by Niche for 2026. Moore was named the 2025 Florida Superintendent of the Year and a national finalist.

Moore said serving as Superintendent of Schools has been one of the greatest privileges of his professional life. He said his belief in the power of public education to transform lives is stronger than ever. Moore said the accomplishments are evidence of what happens when beliefs become behaviors, behaviors become habits, and habits become coherent systems of work.

As Moore enters his final school year, he identified two priorities: ensuring every School District of Indian River County school earns an A grade and positioning the district to become the No. 1 school district in Florida. Following his departure, Moore said he intends to explore opportunities to help other leaders and school systems create conditions for exceptional student outcomes.

cards.headline: Environmental Learning Center in Vero Beach hosts mosquito and insect lecture Saturday
cards.teaser: Jeff Summersill with Indian River Mosquito Control District and two UF professors will discuss insects during a Double Feature Lecture at the Environmental Learning Center in Vero Beach on Saturday.
cards.body:
Jeff Summersill, agricultural pilot and with Indian River Mosquito Control District, and Eva Buckner, UF/IFAS associate professor and medical entomology specialist, along with Panpim Thongsripong, UF/IFAS assistant professor of vector-borne disease ecology, will discuss insects during a Double Feature Lecture at the Environmental Learning Center in Vero Beach on Saturday, Aug. 22, from 12:30 to 2:30 p.m. The Environmental Learning Center is located at 255 Live Oak Drive in Vero Beach.

The lecture is part of the Currents Connections series at the Environmental Learning Center. Additional events this weekend at the center include a Nourish Flourish knife skills class with Chef Stacy Maple on Saturday at a cost of $20 for ages 12 and older, with those under 12 required to be accompanied by a paying adult.

cards.headline: Kuhio Aloy hits first two pro homers as St. Lucie Mets fall 7-3 to Jupiter
cards.teaser: Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets fell 7-3 to the Jupiter Hammerheads to close out a difficult road series.
cards.body:
Kuhio Aloy hit the first two home runs of his professional career Sunday, but the St. Lucie Mets could not overcome a late surge by the Jupiter Hammerheads in a 7-3 loss at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The defeat ended a difficult six-game series for St. Lucie, with Jupiter winning five of the six games. The Mets have now lost seven of their last eight.

Aloy, the Mets' 11th-round pick out of Arkansas, provided the offensive highlight for St. Lucie with a pair of solo home runs.

His first came in the second inning and gave the Mets a 1-0 lead. Aloy went deep again in the sixth, tying the game 2-2.

Jupiter slugger Echedry Vargas answered with another big performance of his own. Vargas hit a two-run homer off Candido Cuevas in the fourth inning to put the Hammerheads ahead 2-1.

After Aloy tied the game in the top of the sixth, Vargas responded in the bottom half with a towering solo home run off Conner Ware, putting Jupiter back in front 3-2.

It was Vargas' second multi-homer game of the series. He finished the six-game set with five home runs and now leads the Florida State League with 21 this season. Vargas is the first Hammerheads player to reach at least 20 home runs in a season since Marcell Ozuna in 2012.

Jupiter pulled away with three runs in the seventh inning. One run scored on a groundout and another came home on an error before Jeremy Almonte delivered an RBI double off Jose Guevara, stretching the Hammerheads' lead to 6-2.

The Mets attempted to rally in the ninth after Jupiter reliever Ian Medina walked four batters. Elian Peña drew a bases-loaded walk to force home a run and cut the deficit to 7-3.

Davidxon Lara then entered for Jupiter and retired John Smith III on a groundout with the tying run at the plate to end the game.

Mets starter Will Watson, who is working his way back from an oblique injury on a Minor League Baseball rehab assignment, pitched three scoreless innings.

St. Lucie finished the day at 17-30 in the second half and 50-63 overall.

The Mets are off Monday before returning home Tuesday to begin a six-game series against the Lakeland Flying Tigers at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie. First pitch for Tuesday's opener is scheduled for 6:10 p.m.

cards.headline: Environmental Learning Center in Vero Beach hosts mosquito and insect lecture Saturday
cards.teaser: Jeff Summersill with Indian River Mosquito Control District and two UF professors will discuss insects during a Double Feature Lecture at the Environmental Learning Center in Vero Beach on Saturday.
cards.body:
Jeff Summersill, agricultural pilot and with Indian River Mosquito Control District, and Eva Buckner, UF/IFAS associate professor and medical entomology specialist, along with Panpim Thongsripong, UF/IFAS assistant professor of vector-borne disease ecology, will discuss insects during a Double Feature Lecture at the Environmental Learning Center in Vero Beach on Saturday, Aug. 22, from 12:30 to 2:30 p.m. The Environmental Learning Center is located at 255 Live Oak Drive in Vero Beach.

 The lecture is part of the Currents Connections series at the Environmental Learning Center. Additional events this weekend at the center include a Nourish Flourish knife skills class with Chef Stacy Maple on Saturday at a cost of $20 for ages 12 and older, with those under 12 required to be accompanied by a paying adult.
